name: OpenVibe.Domains

liveness.means: the process is up and answers HTTP; it checks nothing else

resumes.what: connections, synced zones, proposals and their audit are rows in ov_domains; the price catalog stays in OpenVibe.Host and the net tools in OpenVibe.Tools
a proposal a stop left 'applying' is marked failed at boot with what was applied, so its person can roll it back; a credential is never held outside one call

conditions: automatic: ovhost deploy puts the previous sha back and restarts again when the ready URL does not answer 2xx within ready.timeoutSeconds after the restart (exit 3)
rollback.window: automatic only while ovhost waits for readiness after the restart; manual afterwards, as long as no blocker applies

blockers.none: migration 0001 only creates Domains' own tables (connections, zones, proposals, audit); an earlier release reads none of them

leases.none: no claims: one process serves the site

notes: Port 5070, unit openvibe-domains.service, database ov_domains. The Domains room (plan 2026-10-28 §5.1). v1: one box prices a name across every ending with 1/3/5-year totals (Host's price catalog), TLD pages, and domain info from OpenVibe.Tools' net tools. v2, the control panel: a signed-in person (OAuth client `domains`) connects a registrar or DNS account through its official API, Cloudflare first. The credential is stored as a Network project secret in the person's own project (ADR-056), granted to `domains` for reveal to the provider's origin only, and revealed per call (network.secret.use); Domains keeps its name, never its value. Every DNS change is a proposal (domains.proposal@1) with the record diff, why, the risk and its rollback; nothing touches DNS until the person approves it on the proposal's page or in the Action Center (domains.actions.read, domains.proposal.decide for OpenVibe.Network). A change whose record moved since the proposal is refused as stale; an applied proposal can be rolled back. Answers account export and deletion (ADR-033).

site.name: Domains
site.tagline: Name it, price it, run it
site.what: Every ending and every registrar for a name, with what you will really pay over 1, 3 and 5 years, the renewal traps flagged, and each domain's public history.
